name: Johanan
overview: Johanan was a male member of the tribe of Gad, noted as the eighth Gadite to join David's followers. He came to David at Ziklag, demonstrating his allegiance during a critical time in David's rise. His role is specifically mentioned in 1 Chronicles 12:12, highlighting his position among the Gadite warriors.
namesAndTitles: The name Johanan means 'YHWH is gracious,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:12, does not indicate it was given directly by God but still conveys a significant divine attribute.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Johanan as a descendant of Gad, linking him to this tribal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded for Johanan in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Johanan's significance lies in his early and committed support of David, joining him at Ziklag as part of a group of Gadite warriors. His position as the eighth among these men underscores a measure of leadership or prominence within his tribe. This alliance was crucial in consolidating David's strength before he became king, marking Johanan as a faithful follower during a formative period.
